title: Establish quantized SLI manifest and error-repayment procedure for model endpoints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: We currently describe SLIs for endpoints in prose and a mix of histograms/quantiles. This makes automated enforcement, cross-model comparisons, and multi-region failover decisions brittle. Objective: produce a machine-readable 'quantized SLI manifest' for each endpoint/model variant that defines discrete SLI buckets (availability, p50/p95/p99 latency, token-quality pass-rate) and an accompanying error-repayment protocol that prescribes deterministic remediation actions when an error budget is consumed above threshold. The manifest must be consumable by routing/orchestration systems (smart-router, circuit-breaker controller) and by the Console for visualization and alerting.
goals: Define canonical SLI metric names and units for token-level and request-level signals
Introduce discrete SLI buckets (e.g., availability: 100%, 99.9%, 99%, 98%) to simplify decision logic
Specify error-budget accounting and a novel repayment protocol that allows automated partial rollbacks or synthetic load to restore budget
Provide a JSON schema and generator for per-endpoint manifests and integrate with rollout pipeline
Ship Console visualization of quantized manifests and automated enforcement hooks into circuit-breakers
acceptance_criteria: A published JSON schema (v1) for quantized SLI manifests with examples for chat, completion, and embedding endpoints
Automated converter that emits manifests for 10 canonical endpoint types from current SLI definitions
Circuit-breaker controller accepts manifest and executes at least two enforcement actions (gradual throttling, regional failover) in staging
An error-repayment procedure documented and exercised in a runbook: at least one simulated incident where repayment actions restore >50% of burned budget within configured window
Console shows manifest summary and discrete bucket visualization; alerts trigger based on bucket-to-burn mapping
design_notes: We choose quantized buckets to reduce noisy oscillation in automated policies — routing decisions operate on bucket labels rather than raw quantiles
Token-quality SLI will be measured as 'promptset pass-rate' against a reproducible eval for each model variant; this is an operational SLI, not a model training signal
Error-repayment is intentionally operational (runbook + automated steps) rather than punitive billing — the goal is availability and predictable recovery
We will version manifests (schema v1, v2...) and allow model owners to opt into relaxed buckets for lower-cost variants
Edge case: multimodal endpoints will carry multiple manifests; router must evaluate the 'worst case' bucket when making failover choices
implementation_plan: Week 1: Draft JSON schema and three canonical manifests (chat-general, synth-embed, low-latency-completion)
Week 2: Implement converter (Python) that maps existing Prometheus SLI queries to manifest fields; add unit tests
Week 3: Integrate manifest ingestion into staging router + circuit-breaker controller; run simulated overload tests
Week 4: Write runbook for error-repayment and automate first two steps (priority-eviction, regional traffic shift)
Week 5: Console integration, docs, and staging burn-drill; prepare rollout plan for canary to a subset of endpoints
error_repayment_protocol: Phase 0 - Detection: continuous burn-rate monitor computes 1h, 6h, 24h burn windows and maps to manifest buckets
Phase 1 - Soft mitigation (automated): if burn_rate crosses bucket threshold, apply tenant-aware throttles and increase batching within safe latency SLO
Phase 2 - Regional containment: shift new traffic away from affected region to healthy regions with compatible model variants (manifest-guided compatibility checks)

Phase 3 - Synthetic budget replenishment: run controlled synthetic traffic (low-cost prompts) against high-priority model variants to 'exercise' caches and reduce cold-start amplification, attributed as budget repayment in ledger

Phase 4 - Human intervention / compensation: if automated phases do not restore budget, oncall triggers capacity add (burst), or schedule prioritized replay jobs; document the ride-up sequence in runbook
manifest_schema_summary: fields: endpoint_id, model_variant, sla_tier, buckets (list of {label, metric, threshold, window}), compatibility_tags
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and conversion logic
Staging fuzz test: produce synthetic burn events and assert controller picks expected enforcement action from manifest
Chaos test: region ejection scenario where synthetic traffic is used to validate repayment accounting
Observability: dashboards that map bucket label -> error budget burn and expected next action
rollout_strategy: Step 1: Canary 5 internal endpoints (non-customer facing) for 2 weeks
Step 2: Expand to 20% of low-priority customer traffic and monitor false positives
Step 3: Full rollout for endpoints in SLO Platform project after 1 successful cycle
Backout: manifests are non-destructive; controllers support 'dry-run' mode and operator override
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive repayment (synthetic traffic) could inflate costs — Mitigation: hard cap synthetic QPS and require approval beyond threshold
Risk: Router misinterprets composite manifests for multimodal endpoints — Mitigation: define 'manifest precedence' and fallback to model-owner policy
Risk: Teams game the repayment ledger — Mitigation: synthetic traffic only counts if run in sandboxed controlled patterns and audited by logs
